indicators.title: Credit-to-GDP Gap (BIS, private non-financial sector, Spain)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), credit-to-GDP gap statistics (BIS Data Portal, SDMX)
indicators.definition: Credit-to-GDP gap for Spain as published by the BIS: total credit to the private non-financial sector from all lenders, percent of GDP, minus its long-run trend (one-sided HP filter, lambda 400,000), percentage points. The Basel III countercyclical capital buffer guide; the same source family as the U.S. pair in the main index.

indicators.title: Debt Service Ratio (BIS, private non-financial sector, Spain)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), debt service ratio statistics (BIS Data Portal, SDMX)
indicators.definition: Debt service ratio of the Spanish private non-financial sector as published by the BIS: interest payments plus amortisation as a percent of income, percent. Published from 1999Q1.

indicators.title: Deposit Institutions' Capital and Reserves to Total Liabilities (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 8.32 (deposit institutions' balance sheet, liabilities)
indicators.definition: 100 x (capital and reserves of Spanish deposit institutions — credit institutions and EFCs, BE_8_32.9) / (their total liabilities, BE_8_32.1), percent, quarter-end month. The balance-sheet leverage counterpart of the U.S. Y-9C equity ratios; oriented so that a thinner capital share reads as more vulnerable.

indicators.title: CET1 Ratio of Spanish Significant Institutions (ECB supervisory statistics, proxy)
indicators.source: European Central Bank, Supervisory Banking Statistics (SUP dataset), ECB Data Portal
indicators.definition: Common Equity Tier 1 capital as a percent of risk-weighted assets, percent. Labelled a proxy: the series covers the significant institutions supervised directly by the ECB (SSM) with home country Spain — the large banking groups that hold the overwhelming majority of Spanish banking-system assets — not every deposit institution, and the sample changes as institutions enter or leave significant status. The ECB's consolidated banking data (CBD2) carry the same concept for the full reporting population but the portal series resolved for Spain is this supervisory one; the balance-sheet capital share above remains the full-population leg. Published from 2015Q2, so the gauge is silent on the crisis-era capital build-up it postdates.

indicators.title: Deposit Institutions' Loans to Non-Bank Residents / Deposits of Other Resident Sectors (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 8.33 and 8.34 (deposit institutions' balance sheet)
indicators.definition: 100 x (deposit institutions' loans and credits to non-bank residents in Spain — general government and other resident sectors, BE_8_33.8) / (deposits of other resident sectors at deposit institutions, BE_8_34.7), percent, quarter-end month. The funding gap that defined Spanish bank balance sheets before 2012: a ratio well above 100 means lending funded by wholesale markets and the Eurosystem rather than by deposits. The Banco de España's own stability-report variant, which adds securitised loans back to credit and strips repos from deposits, prints higher; this is the balance-sheet-tables variant, computed from two published aggregates with no adjustment.

indicators.title: Financial Institutions' Total Liabilities to GDP (Banco de España, financial accounts)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Cuentas Financieras de la Economía Española (Boletín Estadístico, tables 2.5 and 2.1)
indicators.definition: 100 x (total liabilities of the financial institutions sector, all instruments, CFEE balance sheet, BE_2_5.2.19, published in thousands of euros) / (nominal GDP, trailing four quarters, BE_2_1.28, millions of euros), percent. The financial-accounts counterpart of the U.S. Z.1 size measures.

indicators.title: Tourism (Travel) Receipts to GDP (Banco de España, balance of payments)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 17.4 and 2.1
indicators.definition: 100 x (balance-of-payments travel receipts — spending by non-resident visitors in Spain, BE_17_4.8, quarterly) / (nominal GDP, trailing four quarters, BE_2_1.28), percent. A structural single-sector exposure, not a cyclical heat gauge: tourism is the largest single export sector of the Spanish economy — about 12% of GDP on the INE tourism satellite account including indirect effects, of which this balance-of-payments series is the directly measurable part. It sits in Size/concentration as the concentration measure of the economy's external earnings base. No counterpart exists in the U.S. framework.

indicators.title: Employment in Hospitality (NACE I) to Total Employment (Eurostat LFS, proxy)
indicators.source: Eurostat, Labour Force Survey quarterly employment by NACE Rev. 2 (lfsq_egan2)
series_id: lfsq_egan2: ES, sex=T, age=Y_GE15, nace_r2=I / TOTAL, unit=THS_PER
indicators.definition: 100 x (employment in NACE Rev. 2 section I — accommodation and food service activities) / (total employment), percent, Eurostat Labour Force Survey. Labelled a proxy, and the employment leg of the tourism exposure above: hospitality is the measurable core of the tourism industries, but it is not the whole of them (it excludes passenger transport, travel services and the tourism share of retail) and it also serves residents, so the share understates the breadth of tourism employment while tracking its cycle. A Spain-specific exposure: no U.S. component concentrates this much of national employment in one visitor-facing industry. Published from 2008Q1 (NACE Rev. 2 back-series).

indicators.title: Top-5 Banking Groups' Share of System Assets
indicators.source: Banco de España, supervision and financial stability reports
indicators.definition: 100 x (total assets of the five largest Spanish banking groups) / (total assets of the banking system), percent.
indicators.pending_reason: The concept is published as a clean machine-readable series — the ECB's Structural Financial Indicators (SSI.A.ES.122C.S10.X.A1.Z0Z.Z, share of the five largest credit institutions in total assets: 40.3% in 1999, 67.4% in 2025, verified against the ECB Data Portal for this build) — but only at annual frequency. The panel's no-fill rule admits no annual series (an annual value carried across four quarters would be filling), so the indicator stays source-pending as a stated decision point: sourcing it is a frequency decision, not a data problem.

indicators.title: Housing Loans to Households to GDP (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 8.19 and 2.1
indicators.definition: 100 x (MFI loans to households for house purchase, BE_8_19.15, quarter-end month) / (nominal GDP, trailing four quarters, BE_2_1.28), percent.

indicators.title: Total Credit to Households to GDP (BIS)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), total credit statistics (BIS Data Portal, SDMX)
indicators.definition: Total credit to Spanish households and NPISH from all lenders (loans and debt securities), percent of GDP, as published by the BIS.

indicators.title: Variable-Rate Share of New Housing Loans (Banco de España, TEDR new-business volumes)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 19.12 (TEDR new business by initial rate fixation)
indicators.definition: 100 x (new housing-loan volume with an initial rate fixation of up to one year, BE_19_12.3) / (total new housing-loan volume, BE_19_12.2), percent, quarterly sums of monthly new business. The Spanish mortgage-risk gauge that replaces the U.S. GSE/FICO block: most Spanish mortgages reset off 12-month Euribor, so the fixation share measures how much of the new stock reprices within a year of a rate rise. The ECB MIR dataset publishes Spain's new-business rates by fixation period but not the volumes by fixation period; the Banco de España TEDR volume table is the route for the share.

indicators.title: Consumer Credit to Households to GDP (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 8.19 and 2.1
indicators.definition: 100 x (MFI consumer credit to households, BE_8_19.11, quarter-end month) / (nominal GDP, trailing four quarters, BE_2_1.28), percent.

indicators.title: Employees on Temporary Contracts, Share of All Employees (Eurostat LFS)
indicators.source: Eurostat, Labour Force Survey (lfsq_etpga)
indicators.definition: Employees with a contract of limited duration as a percent of all employees, Eurostat Labour Force Survey, as published. A labour-market series inside a financial index, placed here on a stated channel: consumer credit is repaid out of household income, and Spain's dual labour market — a temporary share near a third of employees for most of the sample, against roughly a seventh in the euro area — is the structural reason Spanish household income is unusually fragile to a downturn: temporary workers are dismissed first, so an employment shock reaches household debt service faster and harder than the unemployment rate alone suggests. The series is the fragility of the income stream behind the consumer-credit stock measured above, not a credit quantity itself.

indicators.title: Total Credit to Non-Financial Corporations to GDP (BIS)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), total credit statistics (BIS Data Portal, SDMX)
indicators.definition: Total credit to Spanish non-financial corporations from all lenders (loans and debt securities), percent of GDP, as published by the BIS.

indicators.title: Household Net Financial Saving, Percent of GDP (Banco de España, financial accounts)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Cuentas Financieras de la Economía Española (Boletín Estadístico, table 2.7)
indicators.definition: Households' and NPISH net financial transactions (net acquisition of financial assets minus net incurrence of liabilities) as a percent of GDP, as published by the Banco de España (BE_2_7.7, 'ratio sobre el PIB'). Labelled a proxy: it is the financial-accounts counterpart of the U.S. NIPA net saving rate, not the national-accounts saving rate itself; oriented so that lower (more negative) saving reads as more vulnerable. Spanish households were net borrowers of 5-7% of GDP at the 2007 boom peak and net lenders of nearly 9% in late 2020.

indicators.title: Residential Property Prices, Annual Change (BIS via FRED)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), residential property price statistics, via FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
indicators.definition: Four-quarter percent change of the BIS nominal residential property price index for Spain. A price-growth gauge: the level of the index trends, so the vulnerability signal is the boom rate, as in the U.S. panel's price measures.

indicators.title: House Price Index, Annual Change (INE)
indicators.source: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Índice de Precios de Vivienda (IPV)
indicators.definition: Annual rate of change of the INE house price index (national, all dwellings), percent, as published. The IPV starts in 2007Q1; earlier quarters are missing values, never back-filled from another index.

indicators.title: House Price Index to Household Disposable Income per Employed Person (constructed proxy)
indicators.source: Constructed from INE (house price index) and Eurostat (quarterly sector accounts; Labour Force Survey)
indicators.definition: The INE house price index (national, all dwellings, level; IPV769) divided by household gross disposable income per employed person (Eurostat quarterly sector accounts, item B6G for households and NPISH, divided by total LFS employment): IPV index points per 1,000 euro of quarterly disposable income per employed person. Labelled a constructed proxy. The reference concept remains the Banco de España's published effort rate (price of a standard dwelling over gross household income, in its housing-market indicators workbook, which has no machine-readable series route); this construction differs from it in three stated ways: the numerator is a price index, not the price of a standard dwelling; the denominator is income per employed person, not per household, so it also moves with the employment rate; and the IPV starts in 2007Q1 and the employment back-series in 2008Q1, so the ratio enters in 2008Q1, after the boom's peak quarters.

indicators.title: Residential Building Permits, Floor Area (activity proxy for construction credit)
indicators.source: Eurostat, short-term business statistics — building permits (sts_cobp_m); source statistic: Ministerio de Transportes, Estadística de Obras en Edificación (visados de dirección de obra)
series_id: sts_cobp_m: ES, BPRM_SQM, CPA_F41001, NSA, I21
indicators.definition: Index of useful floor area in approved residential building permits (visados de dirección de obra), 2021 = 100, quarterly mean of monthly values. Labelled an ACTIVITY proxy, and the label is the point: the concept this slot exists for is credit to the construction sector (loans to CNAE-F firms), and no machine-readable route to that stock was resolved — the Banco de España's Boletín CSV service carries no activity breakdown, and the ECB's BSI branch estimates (loans by NACE) are published only as euro-area aggregates, with no Spain series (verified against the ECB Data Portal for this build). Permits measure the construction pipeline the credit financed: they led the boom (the index peaks in October 2006 at nearly ten times its 2021 base) and collapsed by more than 95% to the 2013 trough. Where the proxy can mislead: it is a flow of approvals, not a stock of loans — it says nothing about the legacy construction debt overhang after 2008, and it can rise on public or self-financed building that bank credit did not fund.

indicators.title: Bank Lending Survey: Credit Standards for Enterprises, Spain (ECB)
indicators.source: European Central Bank, Bank Lending Survey (Spain breakdown), ECB Data Portal
indicators.definition: Net percentage of banks reporting a tightening of credit standards on loans to enterprises in Spain over the previous three months (tightened minus eased), ECB Bank Lending Survey — the SLOOS counterpart in the U.S. panel. Published from 2003Q1.

indicators.title: New-Lending Margin on Loans to Non-Financial Corporations over the Interbank Rate (Banco de España TEDR, proxy spread)
indicators.source: Banco de España, TEDR interest rate statistics (Boletín Estadístico, table 19.3); OECD interbank rate via FRED
indicators.definition: Average TEDR rate on new loans to non-financial corporations (total credit, BE_19_3.11) minus the euro-area 3-month interbank rate (OECD via FRED), basis points, quarterly mean of monthly values: the margin banks charge firms over the money-market benchmark. Labelled a proxy spread: the reference concept is the margin over a matched-maturity euro swap rate, and no free machine-readable swap curve route was resolved (the ECB yield-curve dataflow, exercised directly in the fifth build, publishes government par yields, not swap rates). The 3-month benchmark is shorter than the average new loan, so the margin also carries a term-premium component that widens when the curve steepens; it is a price-of-credit gauge, not a pure credit spread. It is a bank-lending margin, not a corporate bond spread — the bond-market concept remains source-pending in its own component. The TEDR statistics begin in June 2010, so the margin enters in 2010Q2: it covers the crisis repricing (its peak, about 350 basis points, is 2013Q4) but not the boom.

indicators.title: MFI Debt Securities Issued to Total Liabilities (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 8.3 (MFI balance sheet, liabilities)
indicators.definition: 100 x (debt securities issued by Spanish MFIs, BE_8_3.8) / (total MFI liabilities, BE_8_3.1), percent, quarter-end month: the market-funded share of the balance sheet (cédulas, senior and securitisation bonds).

indicators.title: Net Borrowing from the Eurosystem to Total MFI Liabilities (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 7.3 and 8.3
indicators.definition: 100 x (Banco de España loans and credits to MFIs resident in Spain — monetary-policy lending, BE_7_3.4) / (total MFI liabilities, BE_8_3.1), percent, quarter-end month. The Spanish twist on the U.S. wholesale-funding component: when market funding closed in 2011-12 and again in 2020, the Eurosystem replaced it, so central-bank borrowing is part of the funding-fragility measure, not a separate story.

indicators.title: 10-Year Bono–Bund Spread (OECD via FRED)
indicators.source: OECD long-term interest rates via FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
indicators.definition: Quarterly mean of the monthly spread between the Spanish 10-year government bond yield (IRLTLT01ESM156N) and the German 10-year yield (IRLTLT01DEM156N), in basis points. The price leg of the sovereign–bank nexus: the U.S. index has no counterpart because the Treasury is the safe asset.

indicators.title: Credit Institutions' Holdings of Spanish General Government Debt Securities to Capital and Reserves (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 8.5 and 8.3
indicators.definition: 100 x (debt securities issued by Spanish general government held by MFIs other than the Banco de España — the OIFM aggregate of credit institutions, BE_8_5.6) / (capital and reserves of the same institutions, BE_8_3.9), percent, quarter-end month. The quantity leg of the nexus, measured against loss-absorbing capacity: this is the form in which the loop bites, because a mark-to-market loss on the sovereign book falls on the capital that must absorb it. The first build of this section divided by the total balance sheet instead; the capital-relative form replaces it, for the reason just stated. Loans to government are excluded; this is the securities book that marks to market.

indicators.title: General Government Gross Debt (EDP) to GDP (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 11.5 (EDP debt by subsector)
indicators.definition: EDP (Excessive Deficit Protocol) gross debt of Spanish general government as a percent of GDP, as published by the Banco de España (BE_11_5.11), percent. The stock leg of the nexus: the U.S. index carries no sovereign-debt component because U.S. vulnerability does not run through the sovereign's own balance sheet; in Spain it does, and the debt stock is what the spread is pricing.

indicators.title: Regional Government (Comunidades Autónomas) Debt (EDP) to GDP (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 11.5 (EDP debt by subsector)
indicators.definition: EDP gross debt of the Spanish regional governments (Comunidades Autónomas) as a percent of national GDP, as published by the Banco de España (BE_11_5.13), percent. A Spain singularity with no counterpart in the U.S. panel in this form: the regions deliver health and education, borrow in their own name, and when markets closed to them in 2012-13 were refinanced through the central government's regional liquidity fund (FLA), which moved the risk rather than removing it.

indicators.title: General Government Interest Payments to Total Revenue (Eurostat, quarterly government accounts)
indicators.source: Eurostat, quarterly non-financial accounts for general government (gov_10q_ggnfa)
indicators.definition: 100 x (general government interest expenditure, ESA 2010 item D.41, trailing four quarters) / (total general government revenue, item TR, trailing four quarters), percent. The flow cost of the debt stock: the share of each year's revenue committed to creditors before any policy is funded. Debt can be rolled while revenue covers the interest; this ratio is where that stops being true.

indicators.title: General Government Debt (EDP) Held by Non-Residents, Share of Total (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 11.13 (EDP debt by holder)
indicators.definition: 100 x (general government EDP debt held by the rest of the world, BE_11_13.6) / (total general government EDP debt, BE_11_13.1), percent, quarter-end stocks. The external-dependence leg of the nexus, and the holder-side counterpart of the spread: a sovereign funded by non-residents is exposed to holders with no domestic reason to stay. The measured shape is the flight channel itself: the share was at its highest, about 51%, in 2007; foreign holders then sold through the spread crisis and the share troughed at roughly a third around 2012, with domestic banks and later the Eurosystem absorbing the stock; it recovered as foreign demand returned and stands near its 2007 level again — the dependence the crisis exposed was rebuilt, not retired. Its sign is not ambiguous in this slot: it measures who must be persuaded to roll the stock over, not whether the price is fair.

indicators.title: General Government Debt (EDP) Held by the Banco de España, Share of Total (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 11.13 (EDP debt by holder)
indicators.definition: 100 x (general government EDP debt held by the Banco de España, BE_11_13.4) / (total general government EDP debt, BE_11_13.1), percent, quarter-end stocks. The Banco de España holds the Eurosystem's asset-purchase portfolio of Spanish sovereign debt (APP/PEPP), so this share is Spain's dependence on official European financing made visible as a stock: negligible before 2015, it rose through the purchase programmes to over a quarter of the debt at the 2022 peak (28%). It is oriented as dependence, consistent with this index's treatment of Eurosystem borrowing in the funding component — with the offset stated plainly: a captive official holder also stabilises the market it dominates, and the gauge reads the dependence, not the net of the two. The two readings diverge exactly when purchases stop and the share must be re-absorbed by price-sensitive holders.

indicators.title: General Government Debt (EDP) with Residual Maturity up to One Year, Share of Total (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 11.13 (EDP debt by instrument and residual maturity)
indicators.definition: 100 x (EDP debt in securities with residual maturity up to one year, BE_11_13.9, plus EDP loans with residual maturity up to one year, BE_11_13.10) / (total EDP debt, BE_11_13.1), percent, quarter-end stocks. The refinancing-structure leg: the share of the stock that must be rolled within a year is the speed at which a funding strike reaches the sovereign, whatever the average maturity of the whole stock. The Tesoro Público publishes the average life of state debt monthly, but as dated report files with no stable series route; this residual-maturity share is the same risk read from the Banco de España's holder-and-maturity table, on the panel's quarterly convention.

indicators.title: Net International Investment Position to GDP (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, tables 17.21 (international investment position) and 2.1
indicators.definition: 100 x (net international investment position — Spanish residents' financial assets abroad minus foreign holdings of Spanish liabilities, all sectors, BE_17_21.1, quarter-end stock) / (nominal GDP, trailing four quarters, BE_2_1.28), percent; oriented so that a more negative position reads as more vulnerable. A first-order Spain gauge with no counterpart in the U.S. panel: Spain ran persistent current-account deficits through the boom and financed them abroad, so the whole economy — not only the sovereign — entered the crisis owing the rest of the world close to a year's GDP: the position sat between -85% and -97% of GDP from 2007 to the mid-2010s (the trough, -97%, is end-2009, where the fallen GDP denominator compounds the stock) and has since improved to about -40%. It sits in the nexus component because that is where this index keeps the external-funding legs: the sovereign's holder structure above is the same dependence read on one issuer.

indicators.title: Regional Government Debt Financed by the State Financing Funds, Share of Regional Debt (Banco de España)
indicators.source: Banco de España, Boletín Estadístico, table 13.7 (regional government EDP debt by instrument)
indicators.definition: 100 x (regional governments' EDP debt in loans from the state financing funds — the Fondo de Liquidez Autonómica (FLA) and its successor financing funds, BE_13_7.11) / (total regional government EDP debt, BE_13_7.1), percent, quarter-end stocks. The sharp form of the regional leg: the regional debt stock above says how much the regions owe; this share says who funds them. The funds were created in 2012 when markets closed to the regions; the share passed half of all regional debt in the mid-2010s and peaks above 60% in 2024 — the regions had not stopped borrowing, they had stopped borrowing from anyone but Madrid, which converts regional credit risk into a direct claim on the sovereign inside the nexus. The Banco de España publishes the loans as zero before the funds' creation in 2012 — the instrument did not exist — so the gauge enters at zero rather than missing.

indicators.title: Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress for Spain (ECB CISS)
indicators.source: European Central Bank, Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress (CISS), ECB Data Portal
indicators.definition: Quarterly mean of the daily ECB Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress for Spain (new CISS), index 0-1. A market-price stress composite across money, bond, equity, financial-intermediary and foreign-exchange subindices for Spain specifically — not the euro-area aggregate.

indicators.title: IBEX 35 Earnings / Dividend Yield
indicators.source: Bolsas y Mercados Españoles (BME) / ECB
indicators.definition: Earnings (or dividend) yield of the IBEX 35, percent. No Shiller CAPE exists for Spain; a yield is the available valuation gauge, oriented so that a lower yield (richer pricing) reads as more vulnerable.
indicators.pending_reason: No stable free machine-readable series for an IBEX or euro-area earnings/dividend yield was resolved, and the position was re-checked in the fifth build. BME publishes index statistics as report files, not series; its published IBEX factsheet carries returns, not a valuation yield, and BME states that historical information and other formats are supplied through BME Market Data (its paid data service), with redistribution of its website information requiring BME Market Data's prior permission. The ECB route was checked dataset by dataset in the fourth build: the FM dataflow is a security-level market feed (its data-type codelist carries no aggregate dividend- or earnings-yield series for a Spanish or euro-area index), and the SEC accounts carry ESA dividend transactions (D.421), which are flows of dividends paid, not yields. The component stays empty rather than substituting a price level for a valuation yield.

indicators.title: Corporate Bond Spread (euro-area proxy, labelled)
indicators.source: ICE BofA euro-area corporate indices / ECB
indicators.definition: Option-adjusted spread on euro-area corporate bonds, basis points, to be labelled a euro-area proxy on the page: Spain's corporate bond market is too thin for a clean domestic OAS, and Spanish issuers fund at euro-area spreads plus a sovereign-linked premium already measured by the Bono–Bund leg.
indicators.pending_reason: No free, publishable route was resolved, and the blocker moved in the fifth build: the ECB yield-curve (YC) data endpoint now answers from the build network (SDMX 2.1; its par-yield tenors were exercised directly), so a benchmark leg exists — what is missing is the corporate leg. The ICE BofA euro-area OAS family is the standard series, and FRED does carry euro members of it (the Euro High Yield OAS, BAMLHE00EHYIOAS), but ICE's terms as published on FRED prohibit reproduction of the data, and this section republishes its values (the page and the CSV downloads), so that route is not usable here. The ECB publishes no aggregate euro-area corporate yield or spread: the FM dataflow is a security-level feed (its instrument codelist classifies individual bonds, corporate bonds by rating among them), and the YC dataflow is government par yields only; constructing an aggregate from the security-level feed would mean building an index, not fetching a series. The bank-lending margin in Business credit (TEDR over the interbank rate) is a different price and is not substituted for a bond spread; the series ships pending rather than substituting a U.S. spread.

indicators.title: Commercial Property Prices, Annual Change (BIS)
indicators.source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), commercial property price statistics (BIS Data Portal, SDMX)
indicators.definition: Four-quarter percent change of the BIS commercial property price index for Spain (all property types, whole country). Earlier builds recorded this dataset as portal-download only; the SDMX route (WS_CPP) resolves and is exercised here. Two limits are stated on the series itself: the BIS Spain index starts in 2014Q1, so the gauge reads commercial-price momentum only in the post-bust regime — it is silent on the 2007-13 commercial collapse, and its percentile is computed against that shorter history; and the ECB's own commercial property datasets (CPP, migrated to RESC) carry no Spain series — the candidate keys return no observations — so the BIS compilation is the only public route.
